notes: Format-faithful synthetic BILLSTATUS bulk-data fixture for congress 119, covering the hr and s directory listings together (the other 6 types return an empty {files:[]} listing in the test's mock, not fixtured here). listing-hr.json exercises a folder entry (skipped), a non-BILLSTATUS file name (skipped, discovery-time only — never counted as a fetch), and 3 real BILLSTATUS files. BILLSTATUS-119hr1234.xml is the rich case: a sponsor, 2 cosponsors, a latestAction, a policyArea, and a <titles> list whose nested alternate <title> must not be picked over the top-level one. BILLSTATUS-119hr5678.xml is the sparse case: no cosponsors/latestAction/policyArea (all null/zero), a CDATA-wrapped title, and a full-timestamp introducedDate sliced to a date. BILLSTATUS-119hr9999.xml has no <title> and is a deliberate parse failure (skip-and-count, never stored). listing-s.json + BILLSTATUS-119s200.xml is the second bill type, proving per-type watermark/fingerprint independence: an empty-but-present <cosponsors></cosponsors> (0, not a failure) and a normal populated bill otherwise.
